class_id: a shell script that hands `redis-cli` a `redis://:password@host` URL (no username segment) gets rejected with WRONGPASS while an application Redis client using the identical URL authenticates fine, because redis-cli's own URL parser treats the empty segment before `:password@` as a literal username of `""` and sends `AUTH "" password` instead of `AUTH password`
feature: any shell script that reads the cycle/distributed lock state via `redis-cli -u "$REDIS_URL"` where the URL is the standard `redis://:<password>@<host>:<port>[/<db>]` form with no username (scraper-wake.sh's lock-TTL read, deploy-linux.sh's cycle-lock release path)
symptom: every shell-side redis-cli read against a password-only URL failed with WRONGPASS / 'NOAUTH Authentication required', so every scraper-wake invocation treated the cycle lock as unreadable and proceeded fail-open (skipping the lock check entirely) rather than failing safe, while the Node.js application (ioredis) reading the SAME URL from the SAME box authenticated with 0 errors across 674,546 cache hits in the same window — a discrepancy that reads as 'the app's credentials are fine so the URL must be fine' when the actual defect is redis-cli's own username-parsing behaviour (cli_common.c:341-343 in redis-cli 7.0.15: a `:` before `@` with nothing preceding it is parsed as an empty-string username, not 'no username'). Measured 2026-09-27/28, IPODhan (#719): 22 of 22 staging wakes read 'lock-read-unavailable ... NOAUTH' before the fix; a probe with the real redis-cli binary reproduced the WRONGPASS response from an empty-string AUTH exactly as the RCA predicted. Wider shape: any shell tool that re-parses a credentialed URL string independently of the language runtime's own client library is a second, unaudited URL parser, and the two parsers silently disagreeing (one accepts, one rejects) reads as 'my code is right, the infra must be broken' rather than 'I have two parsers and one is wrong'.
first_seen: 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-27, IPODhan, issue #719 (contract 1): 2 earlier fix rounds (PR #1137) diagnosed 'no password in the URL' and 'REDIS_DB mismatch' — both disproved by direct measurement (staging's REDIS_URL confirmed to carry a password and a /N db path). Root cause proven 2026-09-27 23:31 IST by an owner-approved read-only `redis-cli` probe on the VPS: `redis-cli 7.0.15` parsing `redis://:pw@host` sends `AUTH "" pw`, which the server treats as a real (wrong) username plus password, returning WRONGPASS.
fix_prs: #1252 (2026-09-28): a shared `scripts/lib/redis-cli-auth.sh` sets `REDISCLI_AUTH` (the environment-variable auth path redis-cli supports, which bypasses its own URL username/password parsing) instead of passing a `-u redis://:pw@...` URL; used by both scraper-wake.sh's lock-TTL read and deploy-linux.sh's cycle-lock release. Round 1 review found `@` split at the FIRST occurrence (wrong when a password itself contains `@`) and REDISCLI_AUTH being exported into the deploy shell and inherited by pm2-launched apps (a secret-leak class); r1 fixed both (last-`@` split; no export into the caller).
detection_check: none dedicated to the URL-parsing mismatch itself. The staging wake log's NOAUTH/lock-read-unavailable line count (808 before the fix, 0 after) is the proof signal used for THIS fix, but it is a manual/PROGRESS-log read, not a standing nightly check that would catch a regression (a future script re-introducing `-u redis://:pw@...` against a password-only URL) before it reaches staging.
